items.title: Merck barred from making subcutaneous Keytruda in 8 European countries
items.snippet: With the patent court siding with Halozyme, Merck faces restrictions on a product that won approval in Europe last year.

items.title: Argenx shutters Sjogren's study, losing blockbuster expansion opportunity for Vyvgart
items.snippet: Argenx shares have fallen more than 13% after the surprise futility finding, which overshadowed a mid-stage celiac disease win for a separate asset acquired in the company’s $2.2 billion Forte Biosciences buy.

items.title: Newron reveals 5 deaths in late-stage schizophrenia program as FDA maintains hold
items.snippet: After one patient death prompted an FDA hold this spring, Newron Pharmaceuticals has now shared that a total of four fatalities have been recorded among participants receiving its schizophrenia candidate. A fifth death was recorded among those taking the placebo.

items.title: Despite Zealand asset’s ‘intriguing’ weight loss, analysts underwhelmed by blood sugar numbers
items.snippet: For the second time in a week, Zealand Pharma’s weight loss pipeline has delivered mixed results, this time in a Phase 2 trial for the Roche-partnered asset petrelintide.

items.title: Big Pharma–backed Matchpoint scores $150M series B, advancing autoimmune asset
items.snippet: Matchpoint’s lead asset is the oral T cell modulator MPT-062, which the biotech plans to advance into clinical development for autoimmune and inflammatory conditions next year.

items.title: Caribou to stop R&D work, start ‘substantial’ job cuts
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Beyond equity: Why venture debt is reshaping European biotech
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from Jennifer McMahon, partner at Seroba and Joey Mason, venture partner at Claret Capital. We dig into how venture debt buys time when equity can’t and how Europe’s funding gaps, tranching habits and slower urgency shape who uses it well.

items.title: On the move: 4 rare disease companies hiring now
items.snippet: Biotechs developing therapeutics to treat rare diseases include two that received FDA approvals this year for drugs to treat spinal muscular atrophy and Alexander disease.

items.title: Q3 layoffs down YOY, with 90% fewer biopharma employees affected
items.snippet: Big Pharma companies including Bristol Myers Squibb, Johnson & Johnson and Novartis are among those that made or planned layoffs in Q3. Those cuts could affect over 1,800 employees, with New Jersey the hardest-hit state.

items.title: Cerevance Parkinson’s drug shortens 'off time' in Ph. 3, paving path to FDA
items.snippet: The Takeda spinout showed that a high dose of solengepras can shorten the periods during which difficult Parkinson’s disease symptoms like involuntary movements and sleepiness.

items.title: ArriVent sheds nearly half of value on late-stage lung cancer miss
items.snippet: ArriVent BioPharma’s Phase 3 lung cancer trial was clouded by stronger-than-expected data for patients receiving chemotherapy, prompting analysts to pivot focus to a late-stage test of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor in a different type of lung cancer and to the biotech’s antibody-drug conjugate pipeline.

items.title: Biotech VC Forbion raises record $2.6B to support 30 ‘high-potential’ companies
items.snippet: Forbion participated in the November 2025 series B round of Gate Bioscience, which earlier this week inked an up to $870 million deal extension with Eli Lilly.

items.title: Doudna’s CAR T biotech Caribou to end R&D activities, slash staff as financing freezes up
items.snippet: Caribou Biosciences entered the scene in 2011 and went public in 2021. Over the course of its existence, the biotech has received funding and support from a handful of Big Pharma players, including Novartis, AbbVie and Pfizer.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Bayer commits $2.2B to build pharma manufacturing plant in Ohio
items.snippet: The investment will equip Bayer to make oncology, cardiovascular and renal care ingredients and drugs.

items.title: Genmab and AbbVie’s Epkinly win, a rush of deals, Sarepta’s turnaround hopes, more
items.snippet: New data for Genmab and AbbVie’s bispecific antibody Epkinly wowed analysts and could set the partners up for an expanded approval in diffuse large B cell lymphoma; deals have flowed steadily this week, including Novartis’ nearly $8 billion bet on mRNA drugs with China’s Abogen Biosciences; and could Sarepta Therapeut...

items.title: Why executive candidates need the truth, not the sales pitch
items.snippet: The person you expect to address the company’s problems should know the challenges your business faces. Not having that context will limit what they can accomplish.

items.title: 5 biggest venture capital raises of Q3 2026
items.snippet: Venture capital continued to flow into biopharma in the third quarter, though experts pointed out that investors remained selective, preferring to put their money behind advanced and derisked assets, as well as AI-driven drugmakers.

items.title: Shionogi makes $2B rare disease play with IntraBio buy
items.snippet: With its acquisition of IntraBio, Shionogi will gain ownership over Aqneursa, which could hit peak global sales of $1 billion across its two indications in Niemann-Pick disease type C and ataxia-telangiectasia, according to Jefferies.

items.title: FDA extends review of Novo’s hemophilia A drug, citing manufacturing issues
items.snippet: Despite the regulatory delay, Novo is still expecting a 2027 launch for its hemophilia A drug denecimig.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
